content: One Breath at a Time, Inc is a non-profit organization based in Florida, established on August 17, 2004, in Tampa. Its primary purpose is to support individuals undergoing lung transplantation at Tampa General Hospital. This hospital is affiliated with the University of South Florida College of Medicine and serves a population of over 4 million people across 12 counties in West Central Florida. The organization conducts group meetings at the hospital, where various aspects of the lung transplantation process are discussed. These discussions include what transplant candidates can expect in terms of temporary lifestyle changes, strategies to manage anxiety during the process, protocols for adapting to anti-rejection medications, the impact of the recovery period on families, and how daily activities may be affected post-transplant. The organization’s mission, as stated by its president, Angel Oliva, is to assist lung transplant recipients, their families, and their support systems throughout the transplantation process while also promoting organ donation. The U.S. Internal Revenue Service has recognized One Breath at a Time, Inc as a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt charity. The organization’s immediate goal is to establish a Tampa Bay Lung Transplant Home, which will consist of multiple small apartments and single-family residences. These accommodations are intended to provide temporary housing for out-of-town and out-of-state patients and their families during the initial evaluation, clinic visits, check-ups, the transplant procedure itself, and post-operative care. This goal is communicated to the public and media through informational materials distributed by the organization’s directors. The organization’s long-term vision is to create a Tampa Bay Lung Transplant Clinic and Research Institute. This facility would provide patient care, engage in clinical research, and support basic scientific advancements to improve the success of lung transplants. Medical institutions collaborating with One Breath at a Time, Inc will contribute to staffing the facility and funding its daily operations. A spokesperson for the organization has indicated that several fundraising initiatives are underway to support this project financially. Tampa General Hospital has reported a significant increase in the number of lung transplants performed in recent years. In June 2007, the hospital completed its 100th lung transplant of the year, setting a new record for the same time period. The current directors of One Breath at a Time, Inc include Deborah Mylet, R.N., from Tampa, Florida; Ruth Brakora, from Winter Haven, Florida; Gerald Greenier, from Tarpon Springs, Florida; and Angel Oliva, the organization’s president and a lung transplant recipient, from Madeira Beach, Florida. Dr. Mark W. Rolfe, M.D., FCCP, serves as the head of the lung transplant program at Tampa General Hospital and acts as the chief advisor to the organization’s Board. He provides guidance on the current and future needs of the hospital’s lung transplant program as well as the needs of lung transplant recipients and their families. The information provided above was originally published in February 2007 and later reprinted in various forms on the organization’s website, which was created in May 2007 and remained under construction as of July 2007. Permission to publish this information on Wikipedia was granted by Angel Oliva, the president of One Breath at a Time, Inc.
